name: D0 Collaboration
notes: Institution-level membership rows and leadership are out of scope for this wave (person records and rosters are owned by other workstreams); only the published aggregate counts are recorded.

Conflict noted in a 2026-09-17 verification pass: the D0 INSPIRE experiment record's own description field states "At its peak, the DZero Collaboration included 650 physicists from over 80 national and international research institutions from 21 countries" -- larger than the 540/90/18 figures used above from fnal.gov (2014). Both are genuine published figures for different moments (INSPIRE's is an unstated-date peak; fnal.gov's is dated 2014, after data-taking ended); the fnal.gov figures are kept as `membership` since they carry an explicit `as_of`, and this note records the alternate INSPIRE figure rather than silently dropping it.

summary.plain: About 540 physicists and engineers from roughly 90 institutions in 18 countries who built and ran the D0 particle detector at Fermilab from 1992 until the Tevatron collider shut down in 2011, and who still analyze the data it recorded.
summary.technical: International collaboration operating the D0 general-purpose detector at the Fermilab Tevatron; per fnal.gov (2014), about 540 members from about 90 institutions in 18 countries, split roughly evenly between U.S. and non-U.S. participants.
